final_proof:
By definition, the category of locales $\mathbf{Loc}$ is the opposite of the category of frames $\mathbf{Frm}$, so $\mathbf{Loc} = \mathbf{Frm}^{\operatorname{op}}$. For any locales $L_1$ and $L_2$, a locale morphism $f: L_1 \to L_2$ corresponds uniquely to a frame homomorphism $f^*: L_2 \to L_1$.

The spectrum functor $\operatorname{Sp}: \mathbf{Loc} \to \mathbf{Top}$ assigns to a locale $L$ its spectrum space $\operatorname{Sp}(L)$. The points of $\operatorname{Sp}(L)$ are the frame homomorphisms $p: L \to 2$, where $2 = \{0, 1\}$ is the two-element frame. The topology on $\operatorname{Sp}(L)$ has as its open sets the sets of the form 
$$ \Phi_L(a) = \{ p \in \operatorname{Sp}(L) \mid p(a) = 1 \} $$
for each $a \in L$. For a locale morphism $f: L_1 \to L_2$, the continuous map $\operatorname{Sp}(f): \operatorname{Sp}(L_1) \to \operatorname{Sp}(L_2)$ acts by precomposition with $f^*$; that is, for a point $p \in \operatorname{Sp}(L_1)$, $\operatorname{Sp}(f)(p) = p \circ f^*$.

The locale of open sets functor $\mathbf \Omega: \mathbf{Top} \to \mathbf{Loc}$ assigns to a topological space $X$ its locale of open sets $\mathbf \Omega(X)$, which corresponds to the frame of open sets of $X$. For a continuous map $g: X \to Y$, the locale morphism $\mathbf \Omega(g): \mathbf \Omega(X) \to \mathbf \Omega(Y)$ corresponds to the frame homomorphism $g^{-1}: \mathbf \Omega(Y) \to \mathbf \Omega(X)$ given by taking preimages of open sets.

The component of the counit of the spectrum adjunction at a locale $L$ is a locale morphism $\sigma_L: \mathbf \Omega(\operatorname{Sp}(L)) \to L$. This morphism corresponds to the frame homomorphism $\sigma_L^*: L \to \mathbf \Omega(\operatorname{Sp}(L))$ given by:
$$ \sigma_L^*(a) = \Phi_L(a) $$
for all $a \in L$.

To prove that $\sigma: \mathbf \Omega \operatorname{Sp} \to \operatorname{id}_{\mathbf{Loc}}$ is a natural transformation, we must verify that for any locale morphism $f: L_1 \to L_2$, the naturality square commutes in $\mathbf{Loc}$. This means we must show:
$$ f \circ \sigma_{L_1} = \sigma_{L_2} \circ \mathbf \Omega(\operatorname{Sp}(f)) $$
Because $\mathbf{Loc} = \mathbf{Frm}^{\operatorname{op}}$, the composition order is reversed, meaning this equality is equivalent to the following equality of frame homomorphisms in $\mathbf{Frm}$:
$$ \sigma_{L_1}^* \circ f^* = (\mathbf \Omega(\operatorname{Sp}(f)))^* \circ \sigma_{L_2}^* $$
where $(\mathbf \Omega(\operatorname{Sp}(f)))^* = (\operatorname{Sp}(f))^{-1}$ is the preimage map associated with the continuous function $\operatorname{Sp}(f)$.

We prove this equality by evaluating both sides on an arbitrary element $b \in L_2$.

For the left-hand side:
$$ (\sigma_{L_1}^* \circ f^*)(b) = \sigma_{L_1}^*(f^*(b)) = \Phi_{L_1}(f^*(b)) $$

For the right-hand side, we evaluate:
$$ ((\mathbf \Omega(\operatorname{Sp}(f)))^* \circ \sigma_{L_2}^*)(b) = (\operatorname{Sp}(f))^{-1}(\sigma_{L_2}^*(b)) = (\operatorname{Sp}(f))^{-1}(\Phi_{L_2}(b)) $$
By the definitions of the preimage and $\operatorname{Sp}(f)$, this is:
$$ \{ p \in \operatorname{Sp}(L_1) \mid \operatorname{Sp}(f)(p) \in \Phi_{L_2}(b) \} $$
$$ = \{ p \in \operatorname{Sp}(L_1) \mid p \circ f^* \in \Phi_{L_2}(b) \} $$
By definition of $\Phi_{L_2}$, a point $q \in \operatorname{Sp}(L_2)$ lies in $\Phi_{L_2}(b)$ if and only if $q(b) = 1$. Substituting $q = p \circ f^*$, this membership condition becomes $(p \circ f^*)(b) = 1$, or simply $p(f^*(b)) = 1$. Thus, the set is precisely:
$$ \{ p \in \operatorname{Sp}(L_1) \mid p(f^*(b)) = 1 \} $$
which is precisely the definition of $\Phi_{L_1}(f^*(b))$.

Since both sides yield $\Phi_{L_1}(f^*(b))$ for all $b \in L_2$, the frame homomorphisms are equal. Consequently, the locale morphisms are equal, the naturality square commutes, and $\sigma$ is indeed a natural transformation. $\blacksquare$
